keyChanges.title: Texas Cybercab registrations climb to 58 after nine new VINs
keyChanges.description: TeslaNorth reports Texas automated-vehicle records added nine purpose-built Cybercab VINs dated September 18 under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC, lifting the Cybercab roster from 49 to 58. The same Tesla Robotaxi authorization lists 390 Model Y units and 448 combined vehicles. TeslaNorth states the TxDMV list shows which cars Tesla authorized for commercial automated operation in Texas, not how many Cybercabs are circulating in Austin's geofence or sitting in a yard. That is a pipeline signal, not verified paid-dispatch growth. Public Cybercab service remains Austin-only two weeks after the September 3 launch, with no-highway and at-grade railroad routing still in force. The August VIN floor of 2,172 units built still dwarfs the 58 Texas-registered Cybercabs, so most production cars are not in the commercial robotaxi roster. NHTSA's sworn FMVSS Special Order is still due September 30.

positive_signals: Nine new Cybercab VINs dated September 18 under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC
Texas Cybercab roster moved from 49 to 58 rather than freezing at the launch figure
TeslaNorth cites a TxDMV sync mirrored on the public FSD Database tracker
negative_signals: Registration is not active paid dispatch; TeslaNorth says the list does not show how many Cybercabs are circulating
58 registered Cybercabs vs an August VIN floor of 2,172 built units
No new city launch; Austin remains the only public Cybercab market
Highway and railroad routing constraints from the prior week are unfixed
NHTSA Special Order on FMVSS self-certification is still due September 30
Single published source for the 58 count; TeslaOracle still cited 49 on September 18

keyChanges.title: Tesla trains Austin first responders on Cybercab crash and fire rescue
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account posted a September 18 video of Austin Metro Police being briefed beside a Cybercab and a Model Y robotaxi, with the caption that first-responder feedback is incorporated into Cybercab design and safe operation. TeslaOracle covered the clip the same day. Cybercab has no exterior door handles and butterfly doors that open upward, so rescue training is operational hygiene after launching a wheel-less two-seater, not a fleet or certification win. TeslaOracle still counted 49 registered Austin Cybercabs in that write-up. No major Cybercab crash or fire is documented in the coverage; unsupervised crash data remains thin. The video does not address NHTSA's outstanding FMVSS Special Order or the Austin routing failures already on the record.

positive_signals: Official Tesla Robotaxi video on September 18 shows Austin first-responder training on Cybercab and Model Y robotaxis
Tesla says first-responder feedback is being folded into Cybercab design and operations
negative_signals: No door handles and upward butterfly doors make rescue training a necessity, not a scaling milestone
TeslaOracle still cited 49 registered Cybercabs in the same article
No documented Cybercab crash or fire; the clip is PR, not incident data
Does not resolve the NHTSA FMVSS Special Order due September 30

keyChanges.title: Flemish Minister Presents Tesla-Supplied Belgian FSD Stats Ahead of Oct 6 TCMV Vote
keyChanges.description: Flemish Mobility Minister Annick De Ridder told the Flemish Parliament that Tesla FSD Supervised logged 24.6 million km in Belgium between June 11 and August 31, with collision risk about 9.6x lower off-highway (1 crash in 9.5M km vs 150 in 146.9M km manual) and roughly 30% lower on highways. Five accidents were reported to the Flemish administration; investigators said FSD was inactive in one and found no FSD link in the other four, all minor low-speed crashes with no injuries. The figures were supplied by Tesla as a condition of Belgium's June approval, not independently measured, and De Ridder framed them as evidence that 'road safety and innovation can go hand in hand' 18 days before the Oct 6 TCMV EU-wide vote. That vote still needs ~65% of EU population; the six national clearances remain ~9% with no yes from France, Germany, Italy, or Spain. Drive Tesla Canada still listed only five EU markets and omitted Slovenia.

Off-highway collision rate cited as ~9.6x lower than manual Teslas; highway rate ~30% lower; 93% fewer AEB activations
negative_signals: Dataset was supplied by Tesla as an approval condition, not collected independently by Belgian regulators — the same conflict of interest Reuters previously flagged in Tesla's EU safety briefings
Five accidents were still reported to the Flemish administration in an ~11-week window; the 9.6x figure is off-highway only
Oct 6 TCMV qualified-majority arithmetic is unchanged: six small states remain ~9% of EU population vs the 65% threshold, with no commitment from France, Germany, Italy, or Spain

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.10 (2026.27.10): identical notes to v14.3.9, 0.2% TeslaFi
keyChanges.description: Tesla started 2026.27.10 on September 19 with an FSD (Supervised) v14.3.10 header, but the FSD bullet list matches v14.3.9 (MLIR rewrite, RL/vision-encoder upgrades, Automatic Collision Evasion on HW4). TeslaNorth notes the body still says 'v14.3.9 includes.' Not a Tesla App and TeslaNorth both say the real add is Cybertruck Vehicle-to-Home with Powerwall, not new FSD behavior. TeslaFi showed about 21–23 cars (0.2% of the tracked fleet) on day one. ACE remains HW4-only. Pothole avoidance is still listed under Upcoming Improvements. Consumer FSD v15 is not in this build.

keyChanges.title: Tesla AUNZ: 160M km FSD, 40% fewer collisions after 1 year supervised
keyChanges.description: Tesla Australia & New Zealand posted 12-month FSD (Supervised) fleet stats on September 18 covering September 17, 2025–September 16, 2026: 160 million km on FSD vs 2.4 billion km manual with active safety on. Tesla-defined major+minor collisions were 1 per 1.78 million km on FSD vs 1 per 1.07 million km manual (40% lower). AEB events fell 66%, harsh braking 90%, harsh acceleration 86%, harsh lateral 76%, horn use 80%. Same week, 2026.28.5 began pushing FSD v14.3.9 to Oceania HW4 (TeslaFi 0 cars). Service is still Supervised after a full year. FSD is ~6% of regional Tesla km. HW3 v14 Lite remains unshipped in AU/NZ.

keyChanges.title: Giga Texas Optimus steel frame nears north beam — still a construction site, not a factory
keyChanges.description: Joe Tegtmeyer's September 17 drone flight shows Tesla's dedicated Optimus building on the Giga Texas North Campus about five column grids from the north perimeter beam, with concrete going in on three upper floors while rebar, footings, and grade beams continue in parallel. Teslarati (Sept 18) framed this as a 'turning point' toward summer 2027 high-volume production and a 10 million unit/year Musk target. TeslaNorth and Humanoids Daily are more accurate: Tesla issued no comment on the steel gap, has not tied a new completion date to it, and still listed both California and Texas Optimus facilities as Construction in the Q2 2026 shareholder update, with no installed annual capacity. A nearly complete skeleton is not equipment install, commissioning, or output. Teslarati's claim that Fremont 'began mass producing' Gen 3 in January contradicts Tesla's own July disclosure (lines being installed, production anticipated later in 2026 for Optimus Academy) and the still-unrevealed Gen 3. High-volume Texas production remains a 2027 story; Tesla has still disclosed zero official Optimus units.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Headlines call a drone steel-frame update a factory turning point. Reality is six-month-old construction still short of cladding, tools, and any disclosed robot output; Tesla's last official table still says Construction.

positive_signals: Tegtmeyer Sept 17: steel ~5 column grids from the north perimeter beam; concrete on three upper floors; parallel foundation work

keyChanges.title: Ningbo Optimus supplier-audit headlines fade as named vendors deny new Tesla inspections
keyChanges.description: SCMP (Sept 18) reported Tesla officials and engineers had begun auditing Chinese Optimus suppliers, naming Zhejiang Sanhua, Ningbo Joyson Electronic, and Tuopu Group via two executives with business ties, and tying the visits to a ramp 'after its release later this year.' Bloomberg confirmed A-share robotics suppliers jumped on a 21st Century Business Herald piece claiming a Tesla team arrived in Ningbo on September 16, started audits September 17, and had already issued orders. That story did not survive first contact with the companies. Yicai: Tuopu said it had not received notification of a new Tesla facility inspection; Sanhua said it was unaware of a new round; Joyson declined to discuss customers. Tuopu did confirm ongoing Tesla R&D presence and cooperation on linear, rotary, and dexterous-hand actuators, with a robot-component base 'ready'; Sanhua confirmed joint-actuator work with a 'major client.' Chinese media also floated a ~50,000-unit 2026 internal plan that is not Tesla guidance and clashes with last week's unofficial 15,000-unit supply-chain target and unverified 5,000-unit order tickers. Tesla did not confirm any of it. Audits and ready actuator lines are prep, not SOP, yield, or a unit count.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Headlines treat a Ningbo visit as proof Optimus is entering mass production with orders already placed. Named suppliers denied new inspections, Tesla stayed silent, unofficial 2026 volume figures conflict (15k vs 50k vs 5k), and Tesla still has disclosed zero units.

positive_signals: SCMP: Tesla is evaluating Chinese auto-parts partners in Zhejiang as potential Optimus suppliers
Tuopu told Yicai it already cooperates with Tesla on linear, rotary, and dexterous-hand actuators and that the robot-component base is ready
Sanhua confirmed work with a major customer on robotic joint actuators; Tesla R&D personnel are routinely at Tuopu's Ningbo auto/robotics factory
negative_signals: Tuopu and Sanhua denied knowledge of a new Tesla Optimus factory inspection; Joyson refused to comment; Tesla did not respond

keyChanges.title: Barclays lifts Q3 delivery estimate to 475k — still down vs Q2 480k, vs Goldman 435k
keyChanges.description: Barclays autos analyst Dan Levy now expects Tesla to deliver about 475,000 vehicles in Q3 2026, above a Bloomberg-compiled consensus of ~466,000 and above his prior 450,000, citing 55% FSD attach as a volume/margin support and Shanghai exports at least 20% of global volume into Australia, Colombia, and Asia ex-China. That note is the opposite of Goldman Sachs’s Sept 16 cut to 435,000 (from 490,000, below Visible Alpha ~456k) on weak US/China/Europe prints. The ‘beat’ framing does not reverse the auto decline: Levy’s own 475k is still ~1% below Q2’s official 480,126 and ~4% below a year earlier; he also says auto gross margin ex-credits including SBC stays flat or below Q2’s 16.3%, and that vehicle fundamentals are ‘mostly an afterthought’ to the AI story. Street is split by ~40k units with no official Q3 production/delivery print — Tesla reported Q2 on July 2, so the Q3 release is due around October 2. China August retail was already 50,047 (−12.4% YoY) with 8-month China retail −12.44%.

Levy argues Shanghai exports (≥20% of global volume) plus FSD attach are offsetting core-market weakness

negative_signals: Even Barclays’ ‘beat’ case is ~1% below Q2 480,126 and ~4% YoY — sequential and annual volume still falling

keyChanges.title: Tesla to run public Megachargers at 3 Forum Mobility CA depots; 330+ Semi reservations
keyChanges.description: Forum Mobility said Sept 17 it is breaking ground on four California heavy-duty EV truck depots adding 30 MW, with Tesla operating public Megacharger sites at three of them (FM Francis in Ontario, FM Adeline and FM Coliseum in Oakland). MCS plus CCS pull-through lanes are specified, with Forum claiming ~60% range in ~30 minutes. FM Santa Fe in Rancho Dominguez holds contracted offtake/reservations for more than 330 Tesla Semis while remaining open to other carriers; Forum also bolted two Tesla MCS Megachargers onto existing FM Harbor at Long Beach. This is a partner-operated charging model, not Tesla-owned real estate, and is distinct from the Sept 15 pre-assembled 1.2 MW Megacharger hardware already filed. It is still ground-breaking, not live public charging, and 330 reservations are not deliveries. Semi Europe remains a 2027 commercial story with no public US retail price or verified weekly Sparks build rate.

keyChanges.title: Tesla reopens Roadster reservations at $50k deposit — still no production date
keyChanges.description: TeslaNorth reports tesla.com/roadster/reserve is live again with a $50,000 fully refundable deposit split $5,000 card today plus $45,000 wire within 10 days, days before the already-filed October 1 Waco reveal. The reserve page does not show a confirmed retail price, production date, or delivery window; reservations are not final until the wire clears. This is a new commercial step versus last week’s teaser date, not a volume product. The next-gen Roadster was unveiled in November 2017; reservation holders have sat through multiple slipped demo/production windows, with Musk previously pointing customer builds toward 2027 or 2028. Headline performance claims (250+ mph, ~620 miles) remain promotional until a production-intent car is shown Oct 1. A $50k refundable hold is not a delivery and does not move quarterly P&D.

keyChanges.title: Tokyo Model Y effective price under $23k after subsidies — export win, not a Tesla cut
keyChanges.description: Bloomberg, via Japan Times and TeslaNorth, says a Tokyo buyer can stack 2026 national CEV plus Tokyo ZEV grants (~¥2 million) on a weak yen and bring a Japan-listed Model Y (¥5.6 million) to about ¥3.6 million, or ~$22,889 — undercutting China list (~263,500 yuan / ~$39,344) and California (still >$36k after up to $3,500). Model 3 can go as low as ~¥3.3 million. Model Y was Japan’s most imported car in H1 2026; units are Shanghai-built, which is the same export engine Barclays is using to paper over US/China/Europe weakness. The $23k headline is not a Tesla price cut: it is subsidy stacking plus FX, Tokyo-residency/registration dependent, and Tesla is advertising the subsidies in a market still dominated by domestic brands. It does not reverse China retail −12% YTD or Goldman’s core-market miss.

positive_signals: Japan Times/Bloomberg: Model Y was Japan’s most imported car in H1 2026; Shanghai-built units are landing
Effective Tokyo Model Y ~$22,889 after stacked subsidies is the cheapest headline Model Y globally
Supports the Shanghai-export offset Barclays cites for rest-of-world volume
negative_signals: Price is subsidy + weak yen, not a Tesla ASP cut; list remains ¥5.6 million before grants
Stacking is Tokyo-specific; eligibility depends on residency/registration, not a national $23k sticker

keyChanges.title: CSISD board briefed on Terafab housing spillover, not Grimes tax base
keyChanges.description: The Bryan-College Station Eagle reported Sept. 18 that College Station ISD trustees heard a Greater Brazos Partnership briefing (Tuesday night) on worker-family housing 12–14 miles from the Grimes County Terafab site. GBP's Jillian Ryan said south College Station, not the host districts, is where houses for rent and sale sit; a Tesla Austin-factory comparison showed the closest district did not grow fastest. Superintendent Tim Harkrider said CSISD is discussing CTE pathways toward Terafab technician jobs at $75,000–$80,000 a year, and that GBP called its own figures super conservative. The plant remains in Grimes County (Anderson-Shiro / Iola JETI), so CSISD does not collect the Terafab abatement. No new Grimes dirt-work, permit, or vertical-construction story appeared this window. Full start is still the Dec. 1 JETI date.

sentiment.rationale: Headline is a neighboring district 'helped' by Terafab. Reality is a briefing with no vote, no tax revenue for CSISD, conservative GBP numbers, and zero new construction or permit progress at the Grimes site.

keyChanges.title: Tesla deploys first Accordion Supercharger: 16 factory-preassembled stalls per truck
keyChanges.description: Electrek (Fred Lambert, Sept 16) reports Tesla Charging posted its first Accordion Supercharger: 16 V4 stalls fold onto one truck, 20% cheaper to install than a conventional site, instant commission with no on-site technician to energize, and a between-space layout for lots that cannot trench a curb-behind cabinet. Tesla Charging's stated goal is to pre-assemble every Supercharger in a factory. That is a real prefab SKU, not a network recovery. Tesla's connector count grew about 17% year-over-year as of Q2 2026 (82,357 connectors across 8,704 stations) versus 35-45% in 2020-21, after the April 2024 charging-team layoff. Q1 and Q2 2026 additions were 2,236 and 2,439 stalls. BYD's 1,500 kW flash-charging buildout (10,000 stations in five months, 20,000 targeted by year-end) is a China-mainly comparison, not a Tesla stall count. One Accordion site does not reverse the Supercharger slowdown or move Q3 vehicle deliveries.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Official Tesla Charging tweet confirms a new prefab Supercharger SKU. Reality is one site plus a 20% install-cost claim, against two years of slower connector growth after the 2024 charging-team layoff.

coverageGaps.title: Tesla AUNZ: FSD Supervised logs 160 million km in first year with local safety scorecard
coverageGaps.reason: Fetched TeslaNorth (Sept 18). Official Tesla AUNZ posts confirm ~160 million km of Supervised FSD vs ~2.4 billion km manual-with-Active-Safety, claiming 40% fewer collisions and 66% fewer AEB events. AU/NZ have been live FSD markets since 2025 — this is cumulative miles and Tesla-defined software safety stats, not a new country approval. Already filed under FSD v15 Software from Not a Tesla App (same official dataset plus Oceania 2026.28.5 / v14.3.9 OTA). fsd researcher correctly skipped the NATA URL as fsdv15-owned.

coverageGaps.title: Tesla deploys first Accordion Supercharger: 16 factory-preassembled stalls per truck
coverageGaps.reason: Fetched Electrek (Fred Lambert, Sept 16). Tesla Charging posted the first Accordion Supercharger: 16 V4 stalls per truck, 20% cheaper install, instant commission, between-space layout. Distinct from last week's 1.2 MW Semi Megacharger hardware. productionDelivery researcher did not consider the URL. Filed as neutral: real prefab SKU against ~17% YoY connector growth after the 2024 charging-team layoff. Medium confidence (official Tesla Charging tweet; Electrek-only write-up).
